verses.1: In Antiochene, there were also preachers and teachers who belonged to the same church: Barnabas and Simeon, also known as Niger. There was also Lukius from Cyrene, along with Manaea, a companion of Herodianus, the fourth ruler. And then there was Saul.
verses.2: And those who serve their lord and fast, they say that the spirit is holy. So, please assign Barnabas and Saul to the task I have called them to carry out.
verses.3: Then, they abstained from eating, prayed, and raised their hands in reverence.
verses.4: So, after being sent forth by the Holy Spirit, they went to Seleucia. From there, they continued their journey to Cyprus.
verses.5: And those who lived in Salamin reported the words of God during the gatherings of the Jews. They also had a servant named John.
verses.6: But when they traveled throughout the entire island until they reached Paphos, they found a man who was a magician and false prophet. His name was Baruch.
verses.7: He was with his companion Sergius Paulus, a very wise man. He invited Barnabas and Saul to listen to God’s words.
verses.8: And the magician Elúmas caused them to tremble. This is because his name is interpreted in such a way that it implies that he wants to get rid of that “trembling” from their faith.
verses.9: Saul, too, along with Paul, received the spirit of holiness and was filled with it.
verses.10: He said, “O full of all kinds of deceit and cunning schemes, son of a traitor! Enemy of all those who uphold justice! Why do you not stop from disrupting the paths of those who are upright?”
verses.11: And now, you see the face of the Lord upon you. But it’s like having blindness, unable to see the sun for a while. Darkness and gloom fall upon him, and he seeks help from those who can guide him.
verses.12: Then, the young man, seeing what had happened, was shocked and became confused during the master’s teachings.
verses.13: After leaving Paphos, those who came to Pauilon went to Perge in Pamphilia. John, however, left them and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.14: They then traveled from Perga to Antioch, along the Pisidia region. Once they arrived at the meeting place on the Sabbath day, they sat down.
verses.15: After they read the law and the prophets, the leaders sent them messages, saying, “Men, brothers, what is your objection to this law? Say what your objections are.”
verses.16: Then Paul stood up and said, “Men of Israel, and those who fear God, listen to me.”
verses.17: The God of this people, Israel, chose our fathers. He raised the people up in the land of Egypt. Then, after they were brought out of there, he led them away from there.
verses.18: And, for forty years, they were scattered in the wilderness.
verses.19: And by dividing the nations into seven groups in the land of Canaan, he divided their lands among them.
verses.20: As before, four hundred and fifty people. And after that, he gave judges to Samuil, the prophet.
verses.21: From there, they became kings. The God gave them Saul, son of Kish, a man from the tribe of Benjamin. He was forty years old.
verses.22: And they made David their king. He also testified that David was the man who would carry out all my wishes. I found David to be a man who truly loved me, and he would do everything I desired.
verses.23: This God, by His command, brought to Israel the savior, Jesus.
verses.24: When John was proclaimed, before his appearance, baptism of conversion was given to all the people of Israel.
verses.25: But when John had completed his speech, he said, “What do you want from me? Am I not worthy of being called a follower? But look, someone is coming with me. I am not worthy of carrying their feet.”
verses.26: Men, brothers, sons of Abraham, and those among you who fear the God of heaven, let this message of salvation be known to us.
verses.27: For those who lived in Jerusalem, and its rulers, ignoring this truth, and listening to the voices of the prophets on every Sabbath day, they were judged guilty.
verses.28: And when they found no reason for Pilate’s death, they decided to have him executed.
verses.29: And when everything related to him was written down, they placed it in a monument, away from the wood.
verses.30: But the God raised him from the dead.
verses.31: He who traveled for more days than those who followed him from Galilee to Jerusalem; those are the ones who now testify to him before the people.
verses.32: And we too will evangelize you about the message that has been given to our fathers.
verses.33: For this very purpose did the Lord fill our descendants with Jesus, as it is written in the second Psalm: “You are my son; I have loved you since birth.”
verses.34: Since he was raised from the dead so that he would no longer be subject to destruction, it was said that David would give you everything that belonged to David.
verses.35: For in another place he also says: “You will not give your body to be seen through and exposed.”
verses.36: For David, being of noble birth, served the will of God. He slept in peace, and he stood before his fathers. But he also saw corruption among them.
verses.37: But what the God called forth did not show any signs of corruption.
verses.38: It is known to you, men, brothers, that because of this your forgiveness of sins is granted. And from all things, you have not been unable to be justified according to the law of Moses.
verses.39: In this way, everyone who believes is justified.
verses.40: So, see that the aforementioned statement does not apply to the prophets.
verses.41: See, you who despise me, you who are amazed and indifferent, know that I am doing something during your days. It’s a task that you wouldn’t believe if anyone told you about it.
verses.42: And they were called upon to tell them these words on the day between Saturday.
verses.43: After the union was established, many Jews and those who respected Paul and Barnabas followed them. They tried to persuade them to follow God’s will.
verses.44: And on the coming Sabbath, almost all of the city would gather together to listen to the words of the Lord.
verses.45: Seeing this, the Jews became filled with envy and began to insult those who spoke against Paul.
verses.46: Pavlos and Barnabas also said, “It was necessary for us to first speak the words of God. For if you reject him and consider yourselves unworthy of eternal life, then we will go to other nations.”
verses.47: For thus has the Lord commanded us: You shall be brought into the light of nations, and into salvation, until the end of the earth’s days.
verses.48: And when they heard the words of the Lord, they honored and respected His message. They believed that those who followed His teachings would live a life of eternity.
verses.49: The words of the lord were spread throughout the entire region.
verses.50: But the Jews persecuted those women who were respected and honorable, as well as those who were important in the city. They also persecuted Paul and Barnabas. They drove them away from their homes.
verses.51: And those who were responsible for carrying the wooden poles came to Ikonion.
verses.52: And the disciples were filled with joy and the spirit of holiness.
